title: Traffic mirroring and shielded canary SDK conventions for incremental rollouts
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: define and ship a set of API primitives and lightweight SDK helpers that enable 'shielded canary' deployments and traffic mirroring for model rollouts. Shielded canary = a canary variant with scoped observability and guarded promotion rules (automated rollback triggers, limited blast radius, and explicit approval gates). Traffic mirroring = ability to mirror a percentage of production requests to a candidate model without affecting response path (zero-latency impact). This ticket scopes the PM-level contract: endpoint shapes, idempotency semantics for traffic updates, permission model, telemetry events, and recommended client helper ergonomics (JS/Python).
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /v1/rollouts creates a rollout with canary and mirror configuration; PATCH /v1/rollouts/:id/traffic updates traffic weights idempotently
SDK helpers published: start_shielded_canary, mirror_to_candidate, adjust_weights_idempotent, promote_variant, abort_and_rollback
Idempotency doc: server accepts idempotency-key header for traffic-change endpoints and returns 409 for conflicting concurrent attempts
Permissions: role-scoped scopes rollout.view, rollout.modify, rollout.approve are documented and enforced in Private builds
E2E: synthetic workload test showing mirrored traffic does not increase tail latency and telemetry shows mirrored hits in separate metric stream
Rolling automation: automatic rollback triggers when quality regression metric (invocations with 'regression' tag) exceeds configured threshold for more than N minutes
api_contract_snippets: POST /v1/rollouts { name, model_variant_ids: [base, candidate], policy: {canary_percent, mirror_percent, auto_rollback:{metric, threshold, window_minutes}} }
PATCH /v1/rollouts/:id/traffic {delta_weights, idempotency_key}  // server applies delta idempotently, returns operation id
POST /v1/rollouts/:id/mirror {target_variant_id, sample_rate, idempotency_key}  // mirrors copies of requests to target stream
implementation_notes: Server will persist idempotency keys keyed by (user_id, rollout_id, idempotency_key) for 24h to avoid duplicate traffic mutations
Mirror path must be asynchronous: run in worker pool and write a mirrored request event to the 'mirror' queue with header X-Redwood-Mirror=true
Ensure mirror path strips or masks PII and sensitive headers by default; mirror hygiene policy to be part of API contract
SDKs should expose simple high-level helpers but allow passing raw API params for advanced use cases
Telemetry: emit rollout.version, rollout.step, mirror.sample, mirror.latency_ms, rollback.reason as tags
rollout_plan: Phase 1: API contract reviewed by Eng + Security (ETA 1 week)
Phase 2: Server implementation + integration tests (ENG-11207) (ETA 3 weeks)
Phase 3: JS/Python SDK helpers + docs + example app (ETA 2 weeks)
Phase 4: Internal dogfood on Redwood console + runbook (ETA 1 week)
Phase 5: Public beta with opt-in teams; monitor metrics for 2 weeks then GA
metrics: Mirror overhead: no increase in p95 production latency attributable to mirroring > 0.2%
Rollback rate: automated rollbacks triggered / total canaries <= 10% (initial target)
Adoption: number of rollouts using mirror features in first 30 days
risks: Mirroring may leak sensitive data if hygiene is incomplete; require default scrubbing and opt-out flags
Race conditions when multiple actors try to update traffic weights simultaneously; solved with idempotency keys and optimistic locking
Customer confusion over shadowed metrics vs live traffic metrics; need clear docs and separate telemetry streams
Permission scope creep: granting rollout.approve to non-authorized users could promote unsafe models
